chapter_title: Concerning the Three Days and the Two Deaths

12.original: [which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning]
12.content: which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning

spiritual_reading:
The first state is the primal origin of all in the human form, the first good that is called forth to engage what is opposed. When that first good descended into the lowest denial and was immersed in it, a saving influx from the Divine was sent, which entered into that immersed good and lifted it up. After this good was raised again, the Divine as love together with the Divine as wisdom arranged all things into right order, both in the higher degrees and in the lower degrees.

Moreover, a glorious mediating presence came forth and took its station in the outwardly manifest reception of wisdom. It made the Divine likeness visible, and it separated genuine wisdom from every admixture. It acted from elevated states of understanding. This continues until the time when the present arrangement of external states is brought to its end, all disordered forms are dissolved, the vast intensity of self-love is let loose for its final use, and the final collective form of what has been gathered into order is raised into permanence. These three operations had their beginning in that first state, when the primal good was sent forth together with a sufficient fullness of operative powers.

In the opposite sense, the first perishing is the active falsity that entered into those operative powers and confused them.

The second state is the time when those who belong to wisdom and remained faithful through conflict will be established in governing truths within a new spiritual condition and will dwell in a renewed ultimate plane of life. They continue in that new condition until the Divine reveals the visible presence of its own likeness above them.

The duration of their abiding in that new condition is equal to the measure of the first state’s endurance under distress. In this manner they are established and rejoice within the renewed condition.

The great third state is when the Divine reveals above them the manifest presence of its own likeness, and it raises them into higher reception, and it receives them into an interior safeguarding of good and truth, and it imparts to them what is of its own life. It can flow into them with heavenly delight and with the gentle sweetness of peace that removes every distress they had perceived; then there is fullness and unending joy. When the Divine mercy satisfies them, it grants them what further perfects their reception, and within that gift they are renewed.

It can also call them again into a state of peace held in potency, and bring their spiritual form to completion in the same fullness as the first ordered states. And it establishes each distinct power within its own state, in its own proper reception. They dwell in the renewed condition within their own ordered states.

And when they dwell in their ordered states, they come into immeasurable abundance forever, beyond time. From then on they do not measure their life by successions, nor by the reckoning of states and their least distinctions, age after age forever. The Divine is not hidden from them from that time onward; rather, the unveiling has been accomplished to them, and the Divine is disclosed to them forever.

These are the three great states, which the Divine has set in order as a complete process.

In the opposite sense, there are two perishing states.

The first perishing is from the time when wisdom descended into denial and was mingled with the dominant falsities, until the time when wisdom is made pure and is separated from denial in the final vast ignition of self-love for judgment and purification. What remains after that separation can still be formed and added into the final collective form that is raised into permanence.

The second perishing is the perishing in which the interior lives of those who are in evil die: when they are deprived of the outwardly shining truths that give understanding in the natural degree; when they are cut off from the living influx by which they receive spiritual vitality; when they are deprived of the very faculty of life that had been present for reception in the world; and when they are separated and cast away from that final collective order and are held fast in their own bonds. Then the corrupted will becomes their torment and their distress, because their works have fixed them into the complete series of those infernal states.

These are the two perishing states. The first is within time; the second is without end. The second is the eternal perishing.

fills.notes: Matches the chapter’s antithetical structure: three ‘days’ (states) versus two ‘deaths’ (perishing states). Here it names the first perishing, i.e., Darkness mixing into the First Man’s powers.
Sets the third ‘day’ as a distinct state, parallel to ¶7 ‘The second day is the time…’.
The third state is defined by the Father’s unveiling. The correspondential translation requires a repeated clause of ‘unveiling his image over them’, not a new topic.

After unveiling, the next act is elevation into higher reception. In the substrate register this is commonly rendered as being raised ‘to the life’ (life as the higher degree), before being received into the treasury.
The line ‘and he gives … his soul’ demands a prepositional turn: the Father imparts something ‘to them of his soul’, i.e., of his own life-substance in correspondential terms.
Completes the idiom ‘of his own soul’, emphasizing that what is communicated is from the Father’s own life, not an external gift.
Before ‘fullness and a joy eternal!’ the sense requires an introductory particle so the phrase reads as a resultant state: ‘a fullness…’.

The unveiling is described as completed ‘once’ (decisively), after which revelation is continuous. This preserves the impersonal, process-register: unveiling as an accomplished act with lasting effect.

fills.fill: which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning
fills.notes: Accepted as fitting the oldest-layer register: impersonal ordering, numbering, and measure. It summarizes the three states as a complete ordered process.

The ‘living soul’ here is the life-faculty present for reception in the world. ‘Had been placed in the world’ preserves the substrate’s impersonal cosmology: life is stationed as a principle, not morally ‘given’.
After being swept away from the Last Statue, the opposite process is arrest and detention. ‘Seized’ matches the correspondential sense of being held fast in their own bonds.
Completes the detention image demanded by the spiritual translation: cast away from the final order and held fast in self-made constraints.
In the oldest cosmological register, the ‘female’ functions as the corrupted will and concupiscence in ultimates. ‘Female of lust’ makes the correspondence explicit without later pastoral moralizing.
Their deeds fix them into the infernal series. ‘Have set them in those three places’ expresses determination by one’s own works into a completed order of states.

assessment: Most gaps are tightly constrained by the chapter’s antithetical architecture (three days versus two deaths) and by the correspondential sequence: unveiling, elevation, reception into treasury, communication of the Father’s own life, satisfaction and renewal. The most uncertain restorations are in ¶9’s compact gift-formulas and in ¶15’s punitive imagery, where the substrate likely used fixed technical phrases now only recoverable in approximate form.
